text:
elaine: quick smoke for customer Marigold 12 they merged mg-lora-payments-v1; after int4 some invoice amounts lose cents or show odd separators. can someone run a short compat + int4 smoke? they sent a 22-example mini-pack.

tom: i'll take it. can you paste a few of the failing examples?

elaine: flagged examples: 
- Amount: $9,999.99
- Factura: 9.999,99 
0

- Total: a59,999
they reported outputs like "999900" or missing decimals in some templates after the merge+quant.

rachel: kicked off eval on runner-6 (rdx-base-3b) with quant=int4, adapter=mg-lora-payments-v1. cmd: 
```
redwood eval run --model rdx-base-3b --adapter mg-lora-payments-v1 --quant int4 --tasks currency-format --samples 22 --out /tmp/marigold-smoke.json
```

eval-bot: queued job e-1849999999-01 on runner-6. est runtime ~5m.

rachel: quick topline: PPL(base)=11.0, PPL(merged)=11.8 (+7.3%). Numeric mismatches: 4/22 (missing cents/round-to-hundreds), token-boundary diffs: 3/22. One case where "9,999.99" tokenized as ["9", ",", "999", ".", "99"] in base but merged predictions drop the ".99" tail.

tom: re-ran with tokenizer_v3 flag (simulate customer's token pipeline): PPL(merged,tokenizer_v3)=11.3 (delta +2.6%), token diffs reduced to 1/22 (only euro-style left).

elaine: ran int8 to isolate quant effect?

eval-bot: queued e-1849999999-02 (int8)

rachel: int8 run finished: PPL(merged,int8)=11.2 (delta +1.8%). Numeric mismatches down to 1/22. So quantization amplifies a small existing bias.

tom: inspected adapter delta norms 1 a few rows in layers 5 and 8 exceed 1.5. Hypothesis: adapter learned coarse rounding patterns (customer said they augmented with rounded amounts). I tried a clamp-merge (clip adapter deltas to [-0.6,0.6]) and re-ran int4 smoke locally: mismatches -> 0/22, PPL penalty acceptable (~+1.4%). gist with temp patch: https://gist.github.com/temp/mg-clamp-2026

elaine: action items: 1) ask Marigold for their tokenizer recipe and augment config (likely rounding augment); 2) add the 22 examples to onboarding-regress/marigold.json label "currency-loss"; 3) recommend tokenizer_v3 or a pre-tokenize remap for thousands/decimal separators; 4) offer clamp-merge as short-term mitigation and recommend retraining without aggressive rounding.

tom: i'll open ticket RW-62020 and attach eval artifacts + clamp gist, ping SE for training seeds.

rachel: note added to runbook: triage steps for currency regressions: compare int8/int4, check tokenizer variants, inspect adapter delta L2 norms, try clamp-merge, add examples to regress suite.

elaine: marking thread as "smoke -> investigate (pending-customer)". thanks all :thumbsup:
